body:
Tail of the multi-account design (, section 7, "B5"): turn `:core` into a Kotlin
Multiplatform module so an iPhone client can reuse it. B0 made this mechanical; this ticket does
the parts B0 tolerated.

* `kotlin("multiplatform")` with `jvm()` (used by `:app`) and `iosArm64`/`iosSimulatorArm64`
  targets; the iOS targets must compile in CI on a Mac, or at least `./gradlew :core:compileKotlinIosArm64`
  is documented as the check the maintainer runs before an iOS milestone.
* Retrofit + OkHttp interceptors → Ktor client with plugins (auth header, protocol header, error
  mapping to the same `ApiError` codes, timeouts, self-signed-cert opt-in on the Android engine
  only). `MockWebServer` tests move to Ktor's `MockEngine` or keep MockWebServer on the JVM test
  source set.
* `javax.inject.Inject` leaves `:core`; `:app` wires the constructors in Hilt `@Provides`.
* `Room.databaseBuilder` factory per platform (`:app` keeps the Android one; the iOS one is a
  documented one-liner on the driver path). Migrations rewritten against `SQLiteConnection` so
  they run on both.
* `AppFormat`/`AppLocale`: check for `java.text`/`java.util.Locale` use and move behind an
  `expect`/`actual` or a small interface.
* Deliverable: `android/core/README.md` describes how an iOS app consumes the module and which
  interfaces it has to implement (`SecretStore`, `BackgroundSync`, `DeviceId`, database factory).
* No user-visible change; `verify-all.sh` keeps running `:core:jvmTest`.
title: Android core goes Kotlin Multiplatform: Ktor, no javax.inject, iOS targets compile (B5)
